Quick triage notes — attaching a short summary of the traffic maps.

What I'm seeing: 
- ThirvemMed's route was on a policy profile that uses a conservative per-window quota (QPS window = 60s) plus a burst credit limiter. Their traffic pattern changed to many short concurrent spikes (client-side fanout after a retry change) which drained the burst bucket.
- When credits hit zero, requests get shaped aggressively which increases latency for queued requests and surfaces 429s for requests that exceed the refill heuristics.
- There was a recent policy rollout (global tuning) that adjusted refill rates for a set of customers in the Healthcare segment. ThriveMed looks to be in that cohort and the applied profile reduced their refill factor by ~30% vs the prior baseline.

Immediate recommended actions (short window):
1) Temporarily bump ThriveMed's refill-rate by 2x and enlarge the burst window to allow their short spikes for the next 2 hours.
2) Open a canary route to a higher-throughput variant of the model instance pool (same model but with relaxed kernel throttling) for 15% of traffic.
3) On the customer side, ask them to roll back the client retry/fanout change if feasible (low-lift ask).

I'll prepare a policy diff and a one-click rollback. Marcus, can you confirm capacity for the canary route?

- Karthik
Staff Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime

Internal team found that a recent policy tuning reduced refill rates for a set of healthcare customers and ThriveMed's client-side pattern drained their burst credits. We've applied a temporary override to bump their refill-rate and opened a canary route to a higher-throughput pool (15% traffic). Early signals (first 20m):
- 429s dropped from ~8% to ~0.6%
- p95 latency back to ~420ms in the canary; baseline pool still recovering as credits refill

- Karthik will produce a postmortem and policy diff that we can share with ThriveMed.
